sections.heading: Core Gameplay Mechanics
sections.body:
At its core, TenTrix is a simple game to learn, but challenging to master. The game's objective is to fill up all the colored grids by dragging blocks into place. Sounds easy, right? Well, it is – but that's where the challenge begins. As players progress through the game, the blocks become increasingly complex, with different shapes, sizes, and colors that require a combination of spatial reasoning and problem-solving skills to place correctly. The game also introduces new types of blocks, such as rotating blocks and blocks with multiple colors, which add an extra layer of complexity to the game.

The game's core mechanic is based on a simple drag-and-drop system, where players can drag blocks into place by clicking and dragging the mouse or using touch controls. The game also features a undo button, which allows players to correct mistakes and try again. As players progress through the game, they will encounter increasingly complex levels that will test their skills and push them to think outside the box.

One of the key features of TenTrix is its ability to adapt to the player's skill level. The game's core mechanic is also supported by a range of power-ups and special blocks, which can be used to help players complete levels.
